Taking cost/TPR (token per request) and the quantization notes. Quick notes from my pass: 
- Monthly cost per 1k active requests is up ~6% MoM; mixing of long-tail seq requests (+5% of total tokens) accounts for ~60% of the delta.
- We saw two spikes on 01/07 and 01/12 attributable to a partner job with unbounded streaming (ACME Health sandbox). I've flagged the job id in JIRA OPS-1123.
- Candidate mitigations: dynamic batching cap and enforce soft limit on streaming token window; estimate impact ~3–4% savings.

Notes:
- The dashboard currently reports p95/p99 measured at ingress. For the QBR we should call out compute tail separately (p95 compute, p99 compute) vs network/ingress. The ACME team cares about perceived latency (ingress-to-first-byte) so we should include both.
- Proposed additional column: p99_kvcache_hit_rate and weight it in the latency appendix. A 5% decrease in kvcache hit rate maps to ~18% p99 increase in compute on our sample workloads.
- I'll produce a small appendix table with the breakdown and a recommended notation for the slides. Target to drop by EOD Mon (1/22).

Team —
I've refreshed the dashboard with incident windows and short RCAs for the two uptime blips in January. Highlights:
- 01/07: partner streaming job exceeded expected connection churn; auto-scaling reacted in 2m but cold-start inefficiency added 120s to p99 for a subset of requests. RCA draft points to missing backpressure on the partner job.
- 01/12: internal rollout caused a proxy rule misconfiguration; fix deployed same day.

Data gaps called out in the deck (page notes):
- Missing per-region kv cache hit-rate over the 99th bucket (we currently have aggregate only).
- No enforced correlation ID on some partner flows (ACME sandbox) — makes tracing across infra layers noisy.

I uploaded the updated PDF to Drive (link below) and added OPS-1123 as the follow-up. Please review the incident language — I kept RCA tentative pending final logs.
